summary.intent: Support a hackathon team building an early-warning/verifier product in front of SAP for a fictional customer (Soony): analyze supplier data and interview transcripts, query the supplier about shipment status, and build an automated phone-call/escalation alert feature for launch-critical issues.
summary.outcome: Clarified ERP vs SAP and the data contradictions using interview notes, merged interview findings into the team doc, confirmed a three-way-match product direction, got consistent shipment replies from Boise in both threads, and built the alerts feature (alerts.py, escalation.py, dashboard Alerts page, Twilio/ElevenLabs webhooks, CLI, tests) committed on a new alerts branch.

repo: Project is ask-soony (src/ask_soony/); supplier mails are saved to data/inbox/mail-N.eml and shown on the dashboard under 'Supplier mail'.
data/notes/ is gitignored and used for local interview syntheses.
Lint config exempts long SQL lines in store.py and now alerts.py from the line-length rule.

Alert feature is layered: alerts.py (criticality, channels: dry run, email, Twilio, ElevenLabs), escalation.py (chain with timeout), dashboard Alerts page with decision buttons, webhooks for Twilio/ElevenLabs, CLI `ask-soony alert raise/list/decide/tick`, and `serve` runs escalation every 30s.
Alert emails are opt-in; dry-run is the default channel.
Everything in erp/ is a SAP export, but only ordering and packing originate in a system; other data is typed into SAP by hand.
The ERP shipment list, Excel tracker and supplier mails disagree; neither list has quantities, so partial shipments are invisible.

code.finding: After an escalation the alert status must be reset to 'notified'; otherwise the next timeout re-calls the same person instead of the next one in the chain.

workflow: Background watcher commands (task-notifications) are useful for waiting on supplier replies without blocking.
A string-replace edit failed because the file had already been auto-reformatted; re-reading the current lines before patching fixed it.
Supplier in this simulation only remembers within one thread, so repeating context in each thread yields consistent answers.
Twilio trial accounts only call pre-verified numbers; prices/terms were not verified and should be checked before signing up.

friction: Interview transcripts were fragmented and low quality, needing a merge step to be readable.
The slide's '2 of 7 steps have a system' contradicted the contents of the erp/ folder, and the IT question slot was already used up.
An edit to make email opt-in did not apply because of auto-formatting, requiring a second attempt.
Boise cannot provide a tracking link or airline name; only planned status is known, so real-time tracking isn't possible.
open_items: Decide whether the alerts branch gets merged or kept separate (user was unsure).
Build a watcher parser for #SOONY-STATUS blocks and a per-line status dashboard (offered, not yet approved).
Write the demo script and UI sketch for the team doc, then build the single-screen UI.
Implement a 'Shipments' page comparing ERP, tracker and supplier status (proposed, not confirmed).
Someone must create a Twilio/ElevenLabs account and put credentials in .env for live calls; verify current prices and terms.
Add 'missing SHIPPED confirmation by planned departure' as a risk signal in the early-warning logic.
Add trust-per-supplier and configurable approval/escalation rules as product requirements.
Verifier-before-SAP comparison (order ↔ confirmation ↔ receipt/scan) is not implemented yet.
